predecessors.name: New Kingdom of Egypt
predecessors.text: the southern coastal plain, Egyptian Canaan until the New Kingdom's garrisons left

successors.name: Neo-Babylonian Empire
successors.text: Philistia annexed by Nebuchadnezzar II in 604

ledger.x: c. 1150 BC: the Philistines hold the southern coast. 'These people are thought to have settled in Canaan around 1175 BC'; an inscription 'dated c. 1150 BC, at the Mortuary Temple of Ramesses III' names them. The first stage was 'limited to the coastal plain, the region of the Five Cities'; the pentapolis is Gaza…

c. 1136: the Gaza district passes from Egypt to the Philistine cities. Ramesses VI page (opened 2026-10-19): 'Egyptian presence in Canaan was terminated during or soon after Ramesses VI's rule', 'with the last garrisons leaving southern and western Palestine around the time' (reign 'c.1144-1136 BC'). The page names…

c. 1000 BCE (bridged): David's Israel takes the northern Philistine lands. The page says David secured his borders by defeating the Philistines and that Philistia became a client state; no year (David 1008–970 on the infobox). All 11 cells lie inside Israel's 1000 shape. [Fix 2026-10-19: restricted to the cells inside…

c. 1000 BCE (bridged): Philistia becomes a client of David's Israel. The united-monarchy page has David expand his sphere to 'control the weaker client states of Philistia, Moab, Edom and Ammon' and defeat 'the Philistines to secure his borders', as the biblical account and with no year (David 'rules from c. 1000 to…
c. 1000 BCE (bridged): the southern end of the inland strip leaves Philistia without passing to Israel. Cliopatria's 1000 shape no longer has this cell and no neighbour's does; page silent.

c. 930 BCE (bridged): the client relation ends when the united monarchy divides. The page puts the division 'in about 930 BCE' ('Jeroboam's Revolt: 930 BCE'); it does not say what became of the client states; mirrors kingdom-of-israel /ledger/9.
c. 900 BCE (bridged): the northern Philistine coast passes to Israel. Cliopatria's shape cut; the Philistia page names no such change and no year.
c. 900 BCE (bridged): the southern coastal fringe leaves Philistia. Cliopatria's shape cut; no state in the neighbour list holds it, and the page is silent.

c. 830 BCE: Hazael of Aram-Damascus destroys Gath. The Tell es-Safi page cites 2010 reports of 'evidence of destruction by King Hazael of Aram-Damascus around 830 BCE'; Gath was 'A large city in the Iron Age'. A one-year contest: Gath was captured again in 711.
c. 830 BCE (bridged): the raid ends in the same year; no occupation is recorded and Gath remained a Philistine city until 711.
734 BC: Tiglath-Pileser III's fifth Levant campaign reaches the Egyptian border.
701 BC: Sennacherib gives Judah's plundered lands to the Philistine kings.
609 BC: Necho II occupies the Philistine cities ('occupied by the Egyptians in 609 BC, under Necho II').
604 BC: the Egyptian occupation ends when Babylon invades.

wars.name: Israelite-Philistine wars
wars.outcome: The Philistines defeat the Israelites at Aphek and Gilboa (killing Saul) and are beaten at Eben-ezer and the Valley of Elah; David then makes Philistia a client state.

wars.name: Sargon II's campaign against Ashdod and Gath
wars.outcome: Assyria installs and removes rulers at Ashdod and captures Gath in 711.

wars.name: Sennacherib's third campaign in the Levant
wars.outcome: Tribute from Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gaza and Ekron; Judah's plundered lands divided among the kings of Ashdod, Gaza and Ekron; Jaffa reassigned to Sidon.

wars.name: Nebuchadnezzar II's conquest of Philistia
wars.outcome: Philistia annexed; Ashkelon and Ekron destroyed (Gaza and Aphek too on the Philistines page).

certainty.note: The Five Cities' territories were never surveyed; every edge, especially the inland and Judah frontiers, is approximate.
